audits.title: An audit of antiretroviral medication offered to patients with HIV attending a district general hospital for outpatient care.
audits.setting: Genito-urinary medicine outpatient clinic, Central Middlesex Hospital (district general hospital), London

cycle1.result: All patients eligible under BHIVA guidelines were being offered triple therapy. Viral load undetectable in 75% of 20 patients on their first established regimen and 36% of 14 patients who had failed at least one drug.

audits.citation: Ivens D, Brook G. An audit of antiretroviral medication offered to patients with HIV attending a district general hospital for outpatient care. Int J STD AIDS. 2000;11(3):193-195. doi:10.1258/0956462001915525. PMID: 10726946.

audits.title: Findings from the first national clinical audit of treatment for people with HIV.
audits.setting: National audit of HIV treatment centres

cycle1.result: 97.6% of patients on ART received three or more drugs; of these 58.9% had viral load <50 copies/mL and a further 18.1% <500 copies/mL; only 19.3% had HIV resistance testing.

audits.other_findings: Most patients started ART at lower CD4 counts than recommended, mostly reflecting late diagnosis; 74.1% of clinicians said the guidelines influenced care.
audits.citation: Curtis H, Sabin CA, Johnson MA, British HIV Association Clinical Audit Committee. Findings from the first national clinical audit of treatment for people with HIV. HIV Med. 2003;4(1):11-17. doi:10.1046/j.1468-1293.2003.00137.x. PMID: 12534954.

audits.title: An audit of antiretroviral treatment use in HIV-infected patients in a London clinic: the limitations of observational databases when auditing antiretroviral treatment use.
audits.standard: British HIV Association (BHIVA) 2000 antiretroviral treatment guidelines
audits.setting: Large HIV treatment clinic, Royal Free Centre for HIV Medicine, London

cycle1.result: Treatment recommended for 77.4% under guidelines; 819 on ARV therapy; 285 not receiving treatment in line with guidelines (including 33 on non-recommended regimens).

audits.other_findings: Almost half of those not on recommended treatment had previously received ARV therapy; the authors note limits of observational databases for auditing treatment.
audits.citation: Sabin CA, Lampe FC, Chaloner C, Madge SJ, Lipman MC, Youle M, et al.. An audit of antiretroviral treatment use in HIV-infected patients in a London clinic: the limitations of observational databases when auditing antiretroviral treatment use. HIV Med. 2003;4(2):87-93. doi:10.1046/j.1468-1293.2003.00141.x. PMID: 12702128.

audits.title: Findings from the British HIV Association's national clinical audit of first-line antiretroviral therapy and survey of treatment practice and maternity care, 2002.
audits.standard: British HIV Association (BHIVA) antiretroviral therapy guidelines; government target of >90% antenatal HIV testing

cycle1.result: 844 (90%) started recommended first-line therapy; 98 (10%) nonstandard regimens; 3 did not strictly meet starting criteria; shortfalls in pretreatment testing of glucose, lipids and hepatitis C.

audits.other_findings: 99 units (88%) used BHIVA guidelines; 31 centres (33%) felt maternity services met the antenatal testing target; some units had waits over 4 weeks for first follow-up.
audits.citation: Brook MG, Curtis H, Johnson MA, British HIV Association Clinical Audit Committee. Findings from the British HIV Association's national clinical audit of first-line antiretroviral therapy and survey of treatment practice and maternity care, 2002. HIV Med. 2004;5(6):415-420. doi:10.1111/j.1468-1293.2004.00246.x. PMID: 15544693.

audits.title: Audit of the management of antiretroviral treatment-naïve HIV patients in Greater Manchester, UK.
audits.setting: HIV services in Greater Manchester, North Manchester General Hospital

cycle1.result: Baseline laboratory tests in 96%, blood pressure in 53%, urinalysis in 25%; 2 NRTI plus NNRTI in 76%; 82% reviewed with bloods within five weeks.

audits.citation: Ratcliffe L, McQuillan O, Higgins SP, Wilkins EG, Vilar FJ. Audit of the management of antiretroviral treatment-naïve HIV patients in Greater Manchester, UK. Int J STD AIDS. 2008;19(6):414-415. doi:10.1258/ijsa.2007.007284. PMID: 18595881.

audits.title: Starting treatment according to guidelines evaluation: a multicentre audit of HIV patients in the UK.
audits.standard: British (BHIVA) and European guidelines on starting antiretroviral therapy

cycle1.result: 52 patients should have been on ART but were not; 23 of these declined despite advice.

audits.other_findings: Information to support earlier ART (CD4 350-500) was missing for some patients.
audits.citation: Reeves I, Premchand N, Schwenk A, Brennan-Benson P, Cumming S, Lee V, et al.. Starting treatment according to guidelines evaluation: a multicentre audit of HIV patients in the UK. Int J STD AIDS. 2013;24(3):243-244. doi:10.1177/09564624124728. PMID: 24400349.
